newsitem.title: USA: Oil union extends Sun Co talks deadline.
newsitem.headline: Oil union extends Sun Co talks deadline.

text.p: The Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers (OCAW) union extended their deadline for talks with Sun Co Inc on layoffs at the company's Marcus Hook, Pennsylvania refinery.
The company "appeared to show some flexibility" on their early position to lay off 235 workers at the refinery, said Art Wilson, international representative for OCAW.
OCAW had said it would negotiate the cutbacks until January 12, when it could legally cancel the contract and walk out on strike at the facility, which has a rated capacity of 175,000 barrels a day.

Sun has sought to cut costs at the Marcus Hook facility and its two-refinery Philadelphia complex. The company has said it lost $44 million in the first nine months of 1996 at the refineries, compared to losses of $37 million for all of 1995.
OCAW has said the layoffs, announced in early December, violated clauses of a contract signed last spring by eliminating safety positions and shifting some staff positions to management.
